workflows.name: Agentic Candidate Intake, Sourcing Routing & Agent Registry Registration

Automation Opportunity: - Scoring pipeline auto-drafts candidate scorecards from the inventory and process-mining telemetry (replaces manual Step 1 collation).
- Registry record auto-drafted from the SIB decision and DPIA disposition (replaces manual Step 4 keying).
Controls: - CTL-616 (ensure controlled execution — AI Lifecycle Operations, Assurance & Value Realization (PA-128.3).)
- operational: registration gate — no runtime identity without a VS-128 registry record
- operational: SIB configure → buy → build routing for every agent proposal
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shadow-agent risk**: teams deploy unregistered automation outside the VS-128 registry, bypassing tiering, ethics review, and the audit trail; mitigated by the registration gate (no runtime identity without a registry record — Step 4) and the W3949 controls-assurance sweep

- **Feasibility-overstatement risk**: intake scores overstate agent suitability (clean demo, messy production data), wasting build capacity; mitigated by the hours × frequency × error × feasibility scoring discipline and the owning team's BPO sign-off at Step 2
- **Sourcing-mismatch risk**: agents built where ERP-native automation (configure) would have met the need; mitigated by the SIB configure → buy → build default order at Step 3
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the sized AAP platform team (OM §5.3, 7 FTE) and existing VS-128 governance roles; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - AAP intake/scoring pipeline fed by the per-workflow Automation Opportunity inventory and VS-133 process-mining event logs
- VS-128 agent/model registry (links to W3931) — the registration gate behind runtime-identity provisioning
- SIB Capability Sourcing Register (configure/buy/build decision record)
- DPIA toolkit & consent records (links to VS-91/W3939); ethics-review case log (links to W3952)
Time Estimate: Scoring cycle ~4–6 hours/quarter plus SIB-pack admin ~2 hours/quarter = ~6–8 hours/quarter; × 4 quarters ≈ **~24–32 hours/year**. Registration & routing ~3–4 hours/agent × ~30–45 agents/year ≈ **~90–180 hours/year**. Total **~114–212 hours/year** (≈0.06–0.10 FTE), absorbed within the AAP platform team.

workflows.name: Agent Shadow & Canary Evaluation, Graduation & Autonomy-Tier Ratification

Automation Opportunity: - Eval harness auto-runs the offline suites and drafts the comparison pack (replaces manual Step 1 execution).
- Sampled-audit queue auto-draws the canary sample per tier (replaces manual Step 3 sampling).
Controls: - CTL-616 (ensure controlled execution — AI Lifecycle Operations, Assurance & Value Realization (PA-128.3).)
- operational: graduation gate — dual sign-off (AAP eval engineer + owning QA analyst)
- operational: tier-scaled sampled audit during canary
- operational: hard-boundary verification (statutory filings, POS/OT, SoD) at ratification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stale-eval-set risk**: evaluation suites drift from the live task distribution, graduating agents that fail in production; mitigated by quarterly eval-set refresh from production samples and the shadow/canary real-baseline comparison
- **Thin-canary risk**: sampled audit too shallow to catch low-frequency failure modes; mitigated by the tier-scaled sampling floor (100% → ≥10%) and auto-escalation on anomaly

- **Boundary-bypass risk**: a proposed agent design reaches across a hard boundary (statutory filing, POS/OT, SoD); mitigated by the Step-5 verification checklist and SIB ratification before any rollout
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the AAP platform team's evaluation/AI-QA and agent-ops roles (OM §5.3); evaluation load scales with the crawl → walk → run rollout and is a Phase-2 depth planning input, not incremental steady-state headcount.
System Touchpoints: - AAP evaluation harness (offline suites, adversarial/regression cases)
- Shadow-mode runtime mirror and canary guardrail engine (limits/whitelists/value caps) with the sampled-audit queue
- Autonomy-ladder tier flags in the VS-128 registry (links to W3931)
- Non-human identity & ERP role model for SoD verification (links to VS-27/W1408)
Time Estimate: Hands-on effort ~11–18 hours/agent (offline 4–6 + shadow review 2–4 + canary audit 3–5 + graduation/ratification 1.5–3; the shadow/canary windows run 2–4 weeks elapsed and are never summed into effort); × ~30–45 agents/year ≈ **~330–810 hours/year** (≈0.16–0.39 FTE), absorbed within the AAP team.

steps.activity: Evaluation/AI-QA runs the offline evaluation: task suites plus adversarial/regression cases per the sourcing-model §12 evaluation gates; pass thresholds agreed with the owning team
Shadow mode: the agent runs beside humans with no action rights; output quality and human-takeover triggers are measured against the live human baseline

Canary: bounded live actions inside hard guardrails (limits, whitelists, value caps) with sampled human audit — 100% of actions at first, easing to the tier-scaled floor (≥10%) as evidence accumulates
Graduation gate: Evaluation/AI-QA engineer and the owning team's QA analyst co-sign the evaluation pack; failures recycle to the owning team with the failure taxonomy

Autonomy-tier ratification: tier assigned per the ladder (Tier 1 human-approval-gated / Tier 2 bounded / Tier 3 autonomous-in-bounds) and the hard boundaries verified — no statutory filing path (BIR/SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG), no POS/OT estate actions, no SoD-conflicting duty combinations; SIB ratifies
Production rollout on the AAP runtime (W5514) with the ratified tier, guardrail set, and kill-switch registered; evaluation pack archived for audit (links to W3949)

workflows.name: Agent Runtime Operations, Guardrail & Kill-Switch Telemetry, Quarterly Re-Registration & Portfolio Sunset

Automation Opportunity: - Telemetry auto-computes drift/takeover/cost-per-task deltas and drafts the re-registration pack per agent (replaces manual Step 4 collation).
- Sunset checklist auto-generated from the registry state (replaces manual Step 5 assembly).
Controls: - CTL-616 (ensure controlled execution — AI Lifecycle Operations, Assurance & Value Realization (PA-128.3).)
- operational: IAP-contract-only tool access under non-human least-privilege identity
- operational: kill-switch with rule-based fallback, drilled quarterly
- operational: quarterly re-registration gate; full action audit trail retained as control evidence
Pain Points / Risks: - **Identity-sprawl risk**: non-human identities accumulate residual privileges beyond the agent's task, recreating the access risk W1408 controls for humans; mitigated by least-privilege role templates, quarterly re-registration, and identity revocation at sunset (Step 5)

- **Silent-failure risk**: an agent drifts (data shift, upstream contract change) and keeps executing wrong actions; mitigated by drift telemetry with auto-escalation, the kill-switch with rule-based fallback, and quarterly drills
- **Cost-creep risk**: agent runs persist after the use-case has faded (the orphan-agent class of W3948); mitigated by cost-per-task telemetry vs the human baseline and the QBR sunset discipline
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the AAP platform team's agent-ops role (OM §5.3); runtime load scales with the production agent count and is reviewed at each QBR.
System Touchpoints: - AAP runtime + tool-contract registry (IAP-published contracts only — no direct database access)
- Non-human identity directory & ERP role model (links to VS-27/W1408)
- Kill-switch controls with rule-based fallback; drift/cost telemetry dashboards (feed VS-135 TBM and the AAP KPI row)
- VS-128 registry re-registration state (links to W3931); incident feed to W3943; audit-trail archive to W3949
Time Estimate: Daily telemetry triage ~30–45 min/working day × ~250 working days ≈ **~125–190 hours/year**; quarterly re-registration ~20–30 min/agent × 40–70 agents = ~13–35 hours/quarter, × 4 ≈ **~55–140 hours/year**; kill-switch drills ~2 hours/quarter × 4 ≈ **~8 hours/year**; QBR prep ~6–8 hours/quarter × 4 ≈ **~24–32 hours/year**. Total **~212–370 hours/year** (≈0.10–0.18 FTE), absorbed within the AAP team.

steps.activity: Runtime operations on the AAP paved road: agents act only through IAP-published tool contracts (never a database directly) under non-human identities with their own least-privilege ERP roles (links to VS-27/W1408)

Telemetry review: drift, error/human-takeover rates, and cost-per-task vs the human baseline (feeds the AAP KPI row and VS-135 TBM); anomaly → auto-escalation; suspected adverse outcome → the AI incident process (W3943)

Guardrail & kill-switch assurance: rule-based fallback verified per agent; kill-switch drilled quarterly; guardrail configuration (limits, whitelists, value caps) change-controlled under the IT change process (links to W1409)

Quarterly re-registration: every agent re-affirmed in the VS-128 registry — tier still correct, boundaries still valid, DPIA/ethics conditions still fresh (links to W3939/W3952); lapsed agents suspended pending re-ratification (W5513)

QBR portfolio sunset: underperforming agents (low task success, negative cost-per-task, owner withdrawal) retired like any product — identity decommissioned, audit trail archived, tool contracts released (the W3948 retirement pattern); portfolio metrics to the QBR (links to W3951)
